items.prompt: Tap the square where the white king stands. (It is the tall piece with a cross on top.)
hints: Find the white pieces: they are at the bottom of the board.
The king is the tall piece with a cross. It stands in the back row, next to the queen.
It is the piece on the right of the white queen, in the middle of the back row.
items.explain: The white king stands in the middle of White's back row, beside the queen. You will soon call this square e1, using a letter and a number.

items.prompt: Tap every square on the same file as the white rook, above it. (A file is a column of squares.)
hints: A file is a column, so the squares you want all lie straight above the rook.
Start on the square just above the rook and go up to the top edge of the board.
There are seven squares: from the one next to the rook to the last row.
items.explain: The rook stands on the c-file, and the two knights beside it block its sideways moves, so the only squares it reaches are the seven above it. All of them share the letter c.

items.prompt: Tap every square on the same rank as the white rook, to the right of it. (A rank is a row of squares.)
hints: A rank is a row, so the squares you want lie side by side to the right of the rook.
Start on the square next to the rook and go across to the right-hand edge.
There are seven squares, all in the same row as the rook.
items.explain: The rook stands on rank 4, and the two pawns above and below it block its up-and-down moves, so it can only slide along the row. All seven squares share the number 4.

items.prompt: Move the white king to one of the four centre squares: d4, e4, d5 or e5.
hints: The king moves one square at a time, in any direction.
Two of the squares next to the king are centre squares.
Step straight up, or up and to the right.
items.explain: From d3 the king can step to d4 or to e4, and both are centre squares. In the middle a king has eight squares to choose from, which is the point of the centre.

feedback_by_move.d3c4: c4 is next to the centre, but it is not one of the four centre squares (d4, e4, d5, e5).

items.prompt: Black to move. The board is shown from Black's side. Slide the rook straight up its file to the square that looks third from the bottom of the picture, counting the rook's own square as the first.
hints: Square names are fixed to the board. Rank 8 is Black's back row, whichever way you look.
The rook is on b8, at the bottom of this picture. The row that looks third from the bottom is rank 6.
Slide the rook two squares along its file, away from the edge it is standing on.
items.explain: b6 is rank 6. From Black's side the picture shows it third from the bottom, so a learner who reads the picture as White's would call it b3. Names count from White's side.

feedback_by_move.b8b3: You read the picture as if White were looking. In this picture the third row from the bottom is rank 6, because rank 8 is at the bottom. Names count from White's side.
feedback_by_move.b8b4: That is rank 4, the fifth row from the bottom of this picture. Count three rows from the bottom: rank 8, rank 7, rank 6.

items.prompt: White to move. Play the written move Nf3. (N is the knight, the piece shaped like a horse.)
hints: N means knight. Find the knights in the back row.
The move is the square it lands on: file f, rank 3.
The knight on the right side of White's back row jumps over the pawns to f3.
items.explain: N is the knight and f3 is where it lands, so the knight beside White's king jumps over the pawns to f3. Next, Black will bring a knight out too.

items.prompt: White to move. Play the written move Bc4. (B is the bishop, the piece with a pointed hat.)
hints: B means bishop. Find White's bishops.
The move ends on file c, rank 4.
The bishop beside White's king slides out along a diagonal.
items.explain: B is the bishop and c4 is the square it lands on, so the bishop beside White's king slides out along the diagonal to c4. The pawn on e2 has already moved, which opened the way.

items.prompt: White to move. Play the written move exd5. (The e-pawn captures on d5.)
hints: A pawn capture starts with the pawn's file letter, then x, then the square.
The pawn on file e is on e4. A pawn captures one square diagonally forward.
The e-pawn takes the black pawn on d5.
items.explain: The e-pawn on e4 captures the black pawn on d5, which stands diagonally in front of it. In writing, a pawn capture begins with the letter of the file the pawn started from.

items.prompt: You set up the pieces and the corner square on your right, seen from White's side, is dark. What should you do?

answer.class: turn the board half way round
options: turn the board a quarter turn
turn the board half way round

claims.statement: In the start position the white rook stands on h1.

hints: a1 is a dark square, and h1 is light.
Each player has a light square at their right-hand corner.
If the right-hand corner is dark, the board is the wrong way round.
items.explain: The light square belongs at each player's right-hand corner, so a dark one there means the board is the wrong way round. Turning it half way round fixes it.
